office_does: A Jefferson PUD commissioner is one of three board members governing the county's public electric, water, sewer and broadband utility; nominated from District 2 (Cape George, Marrowstone, Port Hadlock, Chimacum, Irondale) and elected by the whole county to a six-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat; incumbent Kenneth Collins is not running. Chimacum farmer and Finnriver co-founder Keith Kisler faces Port Hadlock computer-business owner and Navy veteran Michael Brittain, both first-time candidates. Both back more local and renewable power and treat broadband as essential; Kisler stresses conservation and affordability programs, Brittain faster customer service and a review of charges. No rubric axis applies to PUD races.

candidates.summary: Chimacum farmer, co-founder of Finnriver Farm & Cidery and founder of Chimacum Valley Grainery; first run for office. Endorsed by the Jefferson County Democrats and Washington Conservation Action.
highlights: Priorities: stable, transparent rates, grid resiliency and rural broadband [S3]
Wants local generation, solar, wind and storage to reduce reliance on BPA's '250-mile extension cord' [S7]
Would make the PUD's low-income rate program more accessible [S7]

candidates.summary: Port Hadlock owner of two computer-repair stores and Navy veteran (2003-2007) with a wireless engineering background; first run for office.
highlights: Wants faster, accurate answers for PUD customers [S4]
Would review all PUD charges with low-income residents in mind [S4]
Supports expanding reservoirs and exploring ocean, wind and solar power [S4]
No endorsements listed; $1,000 raised as of Oct. 2 [S3][S5]
